title: Short Moving Average
rootCause: n values have n - k + 1 windows of size k. The loop stops at n - k, dropping the last one.

fix.stats.py:
def moving_average(xs, k):
    """Average of every window of k consecutive values."""
    out = []
    for i in range(len(xs) - k):
        out.append(sum(xs[i : i + k]) / k)
    out.append(sum(xs[-k:]) / k)
    return out

wrongFixes.whyWrong: Appending the final window after the loop duplicates the bug's logic outside it. When the input is shorter than k, it emits a bogus average instead of an empty list.

grading.question: How many windows of size k does a list of n values have?
grading.ideal: n - k + 1 (and none if n < k).

grading.question: Which edge cases should be tested for any window function?

turns.text: moving_average([1, 2, 3, 4], 2) returns two values; there should be three.
n values have n - k + 1 windows of size k, and the loop stops one short. I changed the range to len(xs) - k + 1. When the input is shorter than k the range is empty, so it returns [] as before.

transcript.verdict: Approve. The bound now matches the count of windows, and it checked the short-input edge, which a fix that tacked on a final window would get wrong.
